cases.summary: The rider was charged a S$5.00 no-show fee after the driver cancelled. Under NS-1, the fee may be retained only if all three conditions are met: the driver came within 150 metres of the pickup point, waited at least 300 seconds from first coming within 150 metres until cancelling, and made at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling. The contact-attempt condition is met (three attempts: CHAT-01, CHAT-03, CALL-01), but the retrieved evidence contains no GPS data establishing the driver's proximity to the pickup point or the duration of the wait. Without GPS confirmation of the 150-metre approach and the 300-second wait, NS-1 is not satisfied, and under NS-2 the exact paid no-show fee of S$5.00 should be refunded.

arguments.claim: The driver's contact attempts before cancelling are documented, but the NS-1 proximity and wait-time conditions are not established by any retrieved evidence, so the no-show fee cannot be retained.
The rider paid a S$5.00 no-show fee, and the server-computed remedy basis shows refund_no_show_fee is eligible for the full S$5.00 paid amount.

The rider's chat message at 09:03:44Z stated 'Ok, coming in 2 minutes,' indicating the rider was actively en route and only briefly delayed, consistent with the rider's claim of being only a few minutes late.

counterevidence.claim: The driver made three recorded contact attempts before cancelling (two messages and one call), satisfying the NS-1 minimum contact-attempt condition and supporting the driver's statement that they messaged and called the rider.

The driver's chat messages assert arrival at the main entrance at 09:03:14Z and continued waiting at 09:06:44Z, which, if corroborated by GPS, could support a wait of roughly 300 seconds before cancellation.

cases.summary: The driver's no-show fee should be retained. The driver made three recorded contact attempts before cancelling (CHAT-01, CHAT-03, CALL-01), satisfying the NS-1 contact condition, and the chat timeline shows the driver waited from at least 09:03:14 to 09:08:14 (300+ seconds) after arriving. The rider's own message (CHAT-02) acknowledged the driver's arrival and promised to come in 2 minutes but did not appear. The only NS-1 condition not directly evidenced in the retrieved records is the GPS proximity (within 150 metres), which is a missing fact that should be verified before any refund is issued.

arguments.claim: The driver made at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling; in fact there were three (two messages and one call), satisfying the NS-1 contact condition.

The driver waited at least 300 seconds from first contact/arrival until cancelling: driver arrived and messaged at 09:03:14 (CHAT-01), messaged again at 09:06:44 (CHAT-03), called at 09:08:14 (CALL-01), and cancelled after that, exceeding the 300-second NS-1 threshold.
The rider acknowledged the driver's arrival and agreed to come in 2 minutes (CHAT-02) but did not appear, corroborating that the driver was present and waiting at the pickup point.
The no-show fee of S$5.00 was correctly charged and paid, with valid arithmetic and no anomalies.
The driver's long, clean history (2100 days, 4.9 rating, 9100 trips, 0 disputes) is consistent with a legitimate no-show claim, though it is context only and cannot establish fault.

counterevidence.claim: The rider claims they were only a few minutes late and the driver cancelled on them; the chat shows the rider said they were coming in 2 minutes at 09:03:44, which could support a short delay, but the driver still waited well beyond that before cancelling.
The rider has filed 2 disputes in the last 90 days, which is context only and cannot establish fault either way.

missingFacts: GPS data confirming the driver came within 150 metres of the pickup point, which is the one NS-1 condition not directly evidenced in the retrieved records.
Exact cancellation timestamp to confirm the wait duration exceeded 300 seconds from first coming within 150 metres.
Whether the pickup point 'main entrance' matches the rider's designated pickup location.
